notes: Widened to 33 by 0033_ai_provider_chain.expand.sql, which adds the AI provider chain: ai_policies (the per-site chain -- which providers may answer, in what order, and whether the site may send anything off the machine) and ai_egress_log (what left the site, by digest and by size, and never the content). Every table is new, so no row shape changes and nothing that reads the schema today changes behaviour. Widened to 32 by 0032_recording_index.expand.sql, which adds the recording index: recording_segments (partitioned by the segment's start, with its uniqueness in a separate non-partitioned key table because Postgres requires the partition key in a partitioned table's unique index), recording_chains (one row per device per day, holding the head that is sealed into the audit ledger), recording_policies (how long a segment is kept, and the legal hold that blocks its deletion) and recording_segment_keys. Every table is new, so no row shape changes and nothing that reads the schema today changes behaviour. Widened to 31 by 0031_device_address.expand.sql, which adds ONE nullable column to devices -- onvif_base_url, the address the product probes the device at. A binary that predates it reads a database with an extra column it never names, so the column is invisible to it. No row shape changes and no column is dropped or constrained, which is why this is an expand step and not a contract step. The column carries a host and a port and no credential, so widening the window exposes nothing that was not already in the site's configuration. M1 schema window. Widened to 30 by 0030_device_registry.expand.sql, which adds eight NULLABLE columns to devices and creates one new table, device_credentials, with its RLS policy and grant. A binary that predates it reads a database with more columns it never names, so every one of them is invisible to it, and the table it does not know about cannot be read by it either. No row shape changes and no column is dropped or constrained, which is why this is an expand step and not a contract step.  Every release widens the window, never narrows it inside an expand window: the previous binary must remain usable until the matching contract step has shipped and been observed in the field. Widened to 22 by 0022_observation_hosted_attribution.expand.sql, which is expand-only: it drops a NOT NULL and adds columns and a CHECK, so a binary that predates it reads a database with an extra nullable column and ignores it, which is the direction that window exists to permit. Widened to 23 by 0023_site_isolation_for_every_site_bearing_table.expand.sql, which adds NO column and NO data and only creates policies, so a binary that predates it operates on a database with more predicates than it expects and the difference is entirely in whether a cross-site statement is refused. That is the safe direction for an old binary and is why this migration is expand-only: the row shapes are identical, so a 22-era binary keeps working against a 23 database and simply sees the policies its own code already relied on. Widened to 24 by 0024_search_documents.expand.sql, which adds a GENERATED STORED column and a GIN index over it and creates a view. A binary that predates it reads a database with an extra column it never names, so the column is invisible to it, and with one more index the planner may use for a query it does not issue. No row shape changes, which is why this is an expand rather than a contract step. Widened to 25 by 0025_future_partitions.expand.sql, which adds monthly partitions for 2028-2030 to inbox_events and canonical_events and applies RLS policies. A binary that predates it reads a database with more partitions it never names, so the partitions are invisible to it, and the DEFAULT partitions already present ensure the old binary keeps accepting writes. No row shape changes, which is why this is an expand step. Widened to 26 by 0026_camera_adjacency.expand.sql, which adds a NEW table and its RLS policy and no column of any existing one. A binary that predates it reads a database with one more relation it never names, and the relation is written neither by it nor by anything it calls, so the table's rows are invisible to it in the same way a partition is. It is a plan C3 item pulled forward from M6 on ai-and-data.md's recommendation, and it is expand-only for the same reason: no existing row shape moves. Widened to 27 by 0027_event_embeddings.expand.sql, which adds the pgvector extension, the event_embeddings table (tenant_id, event_id, embedding, document, model, created_at) and two indexes. Nothing reads the table yet: it is an expand that awaits the eventsearch free-text reader and the embedding writer in a later contract step. A binary that predates it reads a database with one more table it never names, so the table is invisible to it. No existing row shape moves. Widened to 28 by 0028_incident_threat_score.expand.sql, which adds two columns to incidents -- a threat_score with a CHECK and a threat_reason_chain -- and an index for the attention queue. A binary that predates it reads a database with two more columns it never names, so they are invisible to it, and it writes the incidents it always wrote because both columns have defaults. No existing row shape moves, which is why this is an expand and not a contract step. Widened to 29 by 0029_metric_rollups.expand.sql, which adds a NEW table and its two RLS policies, two indexes and a GRANT, and changes no column of any existing table. A binary that predates it never names metric_rollups, so the table is invisible to it, and with two more indexes the planner may use for a query it does not issue. No row shape changes, which is why this is an expand step.
